usage: Used for plants or leaves that have lost moisture and gone soft, droopy, or dry-looking.
Common in everyday gardening talk; often describes flowers, vegetables, or seedlings that look tired from heat or lack of water.
Can also be used more loosely for something that looks lifeless or lacking freshness, but the main meaning is still physical drooping in plants.
Usually sounds neutral and descriptive; for very small kids or beginner learners, think of it as the opposite of fresh, upright, and lively.
